messages:
customer-qa: We're seeing intermittent 502/504s from the hosted inference API since ~02:10 UTC. This started immediately after we rolled an internal edge-proxy MTU to 1400 in the canary pool. Failures are TLS handshake timeouts, customers hitting the hosted endpoint. Example curl and tcpdump below.

jessica: Thanks — can you paste a failing request_id and a short curl output (no keys)? Also where are calls originating from (region / client IP)?

customer-qa: request_id=abc123-def45, client_ip=34.82.11.90 (eu-west-1). curl output: 
```
$ curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer TOKEN' https://api.redwood.host/v1/models/foo:predict
* Connected to api.redwood.host (10.1.2.3) port 443 (#0)
* TCP_NODELAY set
* TLS handshake timeout
* Closing connection 0
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway

```

customer-qa: tcpdump (client-side) snippet: 
```
12:10:12.123456 IP 34.82.11.90.45678 > 10.1.2.3.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 12345 ecr 0], length 0
12:10:12.123789 IP (frag) 34.82.11.90 > 10.1.2.3: frag 0:1480@0
12:10:12.124012 IP 34.82.11.90.45678 > 10.1.2.3.443: Flags [R], seq 1, win 0, length 0

```

jessica: hmm frag shows up. infra-bot can you check edge-proxy recent config changes and cert rotation windows? :eyes:

infra-bot: Edge canary config: mtu changed to 1400 at 01:58 UTC on canary edge-pop eu-west-1. Cert rotation completed at 01:55 UTC (no errors). No global frontend volume alerts.

sam: this reads like PMTU/IP fragmentation interacting badly with middleboxes — TLS ClientHello getting fragmented and server not seeing it, causing handshake stalls/timeouts. Did the change alter DF/MSS handling or TCP segmentation offload?

customer-qa: we're seeing the client sending fragments, looks like DF=0 on the fragments. Could our NAT or the proxy be reassembling incorrectly?

sam: quick repro commands to ask the customer to run: 
```
# from their client host
ping -M do -s 1372 api.redwood.host   # tests with DF set
curl --interface <ip> -v --connect-to api.redwood.host:443:10.1.2.3:443 https://api.redwood.host/health -o /dev/null -s -w '%{http_code}\n'
# try dig over tcp
dig +tcp @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.host
```

leo: I pushed the MTU change to canary only (eu-west-1) at 01:58 as part of netstack adjustments for a different vendor proxy. That change alters egress path MSS clamping. Rolling that back now to see impact.

sre-esc: Opening INC-2026 for tracking. Action items: capture pcaps from client and canary edge egress, rollback canary MTU (in progress), apply fallback routing for affected customer requests to other eu pop, collect L4 traces and tcpdump at edge, correlate request_id abc123-def45.

jessica: mitigation: rolled back canary MTU change at 03:15 UTC (rollback id rb-240). Temporarily added routing rule to send client_ip 34.82.11.90 to eu-central fallback pop. Asking customer to validate.

customer-qa: after rollback and routing to fallback, 5xx spike subsided. Confirmed several previously failing calls now succeed. We'll keep monitoring for next 2 hours and share pcaps if issue reappears. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:

sam: follow-ups: 1) netops to audit MSS/clamping logic across all egress proxies, 2) engineering to add a quick PMTU/fragmentation probe in our synthetic checks, 3) docs for canary rollback playbook.

leo: noted. I'll file a postmortem if we see recurrence and include exact kernel/tcp offload settings.

jessica: closing thread for now, tracking in INC-2026. If customer sees new failures, re-open and ping #eng-network. :raised_hands:
